claim: *The economics of explicit engineering.* The value of making an obligation explicit determines how much investment it warrants; feasible governability determines how much of that investment can become enforcement. High-value obligations can justify substantial engineering even when they remain judgmental, while highly governable obligations need not be mechanized when little value would result.
topology: Continuous conceptual two-axis space with four quadrants; high value and high governability are independent.
required_terms: Invest in explicit judgment\ value; low governability [3pt]Improve models, knowledge, procedures, evidence, and evaluation.
Invest in enforcement\ value; high governability [3pt]Reliable evaluation can justify machinery with consequences.
Leave judgment informal\ value; low governability [3pt]Ordinary situated judgment suffices; governance is uneconomical.
Mechanize selectively\ value; high governability [3pt]Governability alone does not justify machinery.
bw_encoding: White ordinary nodes and groups; labels and boundaries carry roles without decorative tones.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames. Grayscale refinement: Four investment modes regain distinct quadrant tones tied to their written prescriptions, not a maturity sequence.
alt:
A two-by-two chart. The vertical axis is the value of making an obligation explicit, from low at the
    bottom to high at the top. The horizontal axis is feasible governability — representation, evidence, evaluation —
    from low on the left to high on the right. Upper left, high value and low feasible governability: invest in explicit
    judgment; the obligation matters but the environment cannot yet decide it reliably, so make the judgment more
    explicit and repeatable. Upper right, high value and high feasible governability: invest in enforcement; the obligation
    can be evaluated reliably enough to carry consequences, so build the machinery that enforces it. Lower left,
    low value and low feasible governability: leave judgment informal; it neither warrants explicit engineering nor
    admits economical governance. Lower right, low value and high feasible governability: mechanize selectively;
    governability alone does not justify machinery.
